title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 190 (When agent cannot delegate)

content.overview: Section 190 provides that an agent cannot lawfully employ another to perform acts which he has expressly or impliedly undertaken to perform personally, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, or from the nature of the agency, a sub-agent must, be employed.
content.glance: An agent cannot lawfully employ another to perform acts which he has expressly or impliedly undertaken to perform personally, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, or from the nature of the agency a sub-agent must, be employed.
content.study: An agent cannot lawfully employ another to perform acts which he has expressly or impliedly undertaken to perform personally, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, or from the nature of the agency, a sub-agent must, be employed. Current-law framing: general rule against delegation of personal acts, with exceptions for custom of trade or the nature of the agency.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: An agent cannot lawfully employ another to perform acts which he has expressly or impliedly undertaken to perform personally, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, or from the nature of the agency, a sub-agent must, be employed.

examples.title: Personal undertaking
examples.body: An agent who has undertaken to perform an act personally cannot lawfully delegate it unless the custom of trade or the nature of the agency permits or requires a sub-agent, under Section 190.

hypotheticals.question: An agent has expressly undertaken to perform an act personally. May he employ a sub-agent?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not lawfully, unless by the ordinary custom of trade a sub-agent may, or from the nature of the agency a sub-agent must, be employed, under Section 190.
